change_package: task_runtime.remaining_budgets reports the current counters instead of the initial maxima
the compact system policy tells the model to stop unrelated reads after a relevant match and reserve one call for restricted tests
comparison_caveat: This is a focused follow-up package, not a single-variable deterministic A/B; the arms use independent stochastic Provider requests.
interpretation: The prior arm had one oracle-successful edit that exhausted the tool budget before tests, so Runtime failed. The candidate aligned Runtime completion with oracle success in 14/15 runs.
The fixed eight-call safety budget was not increased, and total tool attempts decreased by one.
Input tokens increased by about 9.0% and model calls increased by five, so the small stochastic sample does not establish an efficiency improvement.
One run still read broadly, searched on call seven, and exhausted the budget without an edit. This remains behavior evidence, not justification for a larger budget or a new privileged tool.
limitations: Three synthetic repositories and five repetitions per case are a small benchmark.
The follow-up changes both budget truthfulness and compact policy wording, so success changes cannot be attributed to either component alone.
Raw artifacts remain under /tmp and are not checked in.
